tour.name: Meteora Private Tour: Monasteries in the Sky, Hermit Caves & Sunset Viewpoints
tour.subtitle: A private day among the rock pillars of Meteora with a licensed guide and car: three of the six working monasteries perched on the cliffs, the old hermit caves, lunch in Kastraki, the best viewpoints and the sunset over the plain of Thessaly. From Kalambaka, or from Athens by train.

tour.overview:
Above the plain of Thessaly, giant pillars of sandstone and conglomerate rise up to 400 metres, shaped by water and wind over millions of years. From the 11th century, hermits lived in the caves of these rocks, and in the 14th century monks began to build monasteries on their summits, reachable only by rope ladders or by nets hauled up by winches. Of more than twenty monasteries, six are still inhabited by monks and nuns. Meteora, whose name means 'suspended in the air', has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988.

This private day shows Meteora with a licensed guide and a car. You visit three monasteries, their frescoed chapels and old winch houses, see the hermit caves, have lunch in Kastraki and drive between the best viewpoints, ending with the sunset over the rocks.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Kalambaka or Kastraki, or Kalambaka station
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; each monastery has 150 to 300 steps

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Great Meteoron.
• Varlaam.
• Roussanou or St Stephen's.
• The hermit caves and the old monastery ruins.
• The viewpoints over the six monasteries and the sunset.

WHY THIS WORKS
The monasteries have different closing days and short opening hours; we plan the route around them so you see three, not just one or two, and we know where to be at sunset.

WHO IT SUITS
Anyone who loves dramatic landscapes, photography, Byzantine art and Orthodox spirituality.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you only have one day from Athens without a night away, choose Delphi; Meteora is best with a night in Kalambaka.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Each monastery closes one or two days a week, and all close in the early afternoon in winter. The dress code is strict: women must wear skirts below the knee (wraps are lent at the entrance) and men long trousers; shoulders must be covered.

days.name: The Great Meteoron, Varlaam, Roussanou or St Stephen's, the hermit caves, lunch in Kastraki and sunset
days.description:
What to expect: the monasteries in the sky in one unhurried day, with a licensed guide, private car, entrances and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel or at Kalambaka station at about 9:00. If you are coming from Athens, the early train takes about 4 hours 30 minutes and we adapt the start. You drive up the winding road between the rocks to the Great Meteoron, founded in the 14th century by Saint Athanasios, who is said to have been carried to the summit by an eagle. It is the highest and largest of the monasteries, 613 metres above sea level. You climb the steps cut into the rock and through a tunnel, and see the church of the Transfiguration, covered in 16th-century frescoes, the old kitchen with its blackened vault, the museum and the ossuary with the skulls of former monks.

Next door stands Varlaam, built in 1541 by two brothers from Ioannina, who took 22 years to haul up the building materials. You see its frescoed chapel, its huge wooden barrel that once held 12,000 litres of water, and the tower with the winch and net that carried monks and supplies up the cliff until steps were cut in the 1920s.

Lunch is in Kastraki, a village at the foot of the rocks – lamb or goat cooked slowly in the oven, local cheeses and wine from Thessaly. In the afternoon your guide takes you to the hermit caves at the base of the rocks, where the first ascetics lived in the 11th century and reached their cells by ladders, and to the ruins of abandoned monasteries. You then visit a third monastery, Roussanou, home to a community of nuns, perched on a narrow rock and reached by a bridge, or St Stephen's, the most accessible, depending on opening days. You end at a viewpoint looking over the rocks and the plain for the sunset, and are back at your hotel at about 17:30 in winter or 20:00 in summer.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Pick-up at your hotel or Kalambaka station.
09:30 – The Great Meteoron (about 1 hour 15 minutes).
11:00 – Varlaam (about 1 hour).
12:30 – Lunch in Kastraki.
14:00 – Hermit caves and old monastery ruins.
15:00 – Roussanou or St Stephen's.
16:00 – Viewpoints and sunset.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Monastery closing days change by season; we confirm the three you will visit when we confirm your booking.
• Photography is not allowed inside the churches.
• From Athens: we can book the train and a hotel in Kalambaka for you.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, three monastery entrances, lunch, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: train from Athens, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we do Meteora as a day trip from Athens?
faq.answer: Yes, by train: about 4 hours 30 minutes each way, which makes a very long day. We strongly recommend at least one night in Kalambaka or Kastraki.

faq.question: How many monasteries do we visit?
faq.answer: Three, chosen according to their opening days. We also see the others from the viewpoints.

faq.question: Is there a dress code?
faq.answer: Yes. Women must wear skirts below the knee (wrap skirts are lent at the entrance), men long trousers, and everyone must cover their shoulders.

faq.question: Are the entrance fees included?
faq.answer: Yes, the entrance to three monasteries.

faq.question: How many steps are there?
faq.answer: Each monastery has between about 150 and 300 steps. St Stephen's has almost none, and we can include it if stairs are difficult.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch in Kastraki. Vegetarian and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the stories of the net lift and the eagle, and the caves. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. St Stephen's is reached by a short bridge without steps; the others involve many stairs. The viewpoints can be enjoyed from the car.

faq.question: Can we take photos?
faq.answer: Yes, outside and in the courtyards. Photography is not allowed inside the churches.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Modest clothes as above, comfortable shoes, and a jacket outside summer: the monasteries are high and windy.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Spring is green, autumn golden, and winter can bring snow and mist around the rocks, beautiful but cold. Summer is busy and hot at midday.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
